The '''1996–97 Scottish Premier Division''' season was the penultimate season of [[Scottish Premier Division]] football before the change to the [[Scottish Premier League]]. It began on 10 August 1996.

==Overview==
The 1996–97 Scottish Premier Division season ended in success for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who won the title by five points from nearest rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] to clinch [[Nine in a row|nine titles in a row]], equalling Celtic's record from the [[1973–74 Scottish Division One|1973–74]] season. [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] were relegated to the [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] after finishing bottom. As champions, Rangers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Celtic were joined by third-placed [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. Seventh-placed [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] qualified for the penultimate [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] as [[Scottish Cup]] winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/tables/sdprem97.htm|title=Scottish Premier Division 1996/97|publisher=Soccerbot|access-date=2008-06-03| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080512101831/http://www.soccerbot.com/scot/tables/sdprem97.htm| archive-date= 12 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

The season began on 10 August with the first goal of the season scored by [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]'s [[Gary McSwegan]] as they drew 1–1 at home to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. The season ended on 10 May with Celtic's [[Tommy Johnson (footballer, born 1971)|Tommy Johnson]] netting a late goal to cap a 3–0 win at home to Dundee United to claim the final goal of the season.

==Events==
* 17 August: [[Ally McCoist]] hits the first [[hat-trick]] of the season in a 5–2 win at [[Dunfermline F.C.|Dunfermline]].
* 7 May: [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] win the title with a 1–0 win at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]

==Play-off==
A two leg play-off took place between the 9th placed team in the Premier Division (Hibernian) and the runner-up of the [[1996–97 Scottish First Division|First Division]] ([[Airdrieonians F.C. (1878)|Airdrieonians]]) for a place in the [[1997–98 Scottish Premier Division]].

Hibernian won the first leg 1–0 at [[Easter Road]], and went on to win the second leg by 4 goals to 2 at [[Broadwood Stadium]].<ref name="Playoff">{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/12324871.Airdrie_captain_sent_off_as_Hibs_secure_premier_division_status_Jackson_at_the_double_on_a_night_of_penalties/|newspaper=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=23 May 1997|access-date=17 February 2018|title=Airdrie captain sent off as Hibs secure premier division status Jackson at the double on a night of penalties}}</ref> Therefore, Hibernian maintained their Premier Division status for another season, 5–2 on aggregate.
